property_summary: For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) the reference increments proposalCount by 1 (so the returned/observable proposalCount after the call equals its prior value plus one); the mutant that omits the increment leaves proposalCount unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the reference implementation always increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (new value = old value + 1); the mutant that omits the increment leaves proposalCount unchanged, violating this property for some inputs.

For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the reference contract increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (so querying proposalCount after the call equals its prior value + 1); the mutant double-increments proposalCount (prior + 2) and thus violates this property for some inputs (any input).

For any input to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount), the reference increments proposalCount by 1 (so proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant increments coolOffPeriod instead and therefore for some inputs proposalCount does not increase, violating that rule.

For any call to newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) the reference contract increments proposalCount by exactly 1 (proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant increments coolOffPeriod instead so proposalCount does not increase, breaking this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) increases proposalCount by exactly 1; the mutant increments coolOffPeriod instead so proposalCount does not increase for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) always increments proposalCount by 1 in the reference; the mutant mistakenly increments coolOffPeriod instead so there exist inputs where proposalCount does not increase, violating this rule.

For any caller/address and amount, calling newGrantProposal(recipient, amount) always increments proposalCount by exactly 1 (so proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant increments coolOffPeriod instead, so there exist inputs where proposalCount does not increase and the property is violated.

After init and creating+finalising a GRANT proposal, finaliseProposal will revert unless the VAULT has ≥10x the grant amount (i.e., grant amount ≤ VAULT.balance/10), which depends on VADER being set so moveUtils etc. don't run — specifically: finaliseProposal succeeds only when grant cap check passes.
